findings.title: Revalidate current direct and transitive read authority on replay and receipt
findings.description: After a successful candidate receive for m depending on dep, revoke dep/read while retaining m receive/read. Fresh receive denies correctly, but same-key receive replay and receipt return the stored result. Replay also succeeds when m/read itself is denied. Replay returns immediately after only direct receive checks; receipt checks only direct revision keys. This violates current dependency read authorization promised by the trusted-host API and makes the idempotency path bypass normal access checks.
findings.required_change: Before returning either prior result, validate current read authority for the original input/base closure and exact final candidate closure within the current database transaction; retain receive authority on receive replay. Do not use mutable heads.

findings.title: Verify persisted receipt identity and request binding before returning it
findings.description: Changing the stored result.origin.worker_ref while preserving result.id and the row request_digest causes both replay and receipt to return the corrupted provenance as if it were the immutable original. Neither path recomputes the content-derived result ID or verifies tenant/actor/request key/request digest bindings. The probe simulates accidental persisted corruption in the trusted database, not an external-authentication attack.
findings.required_change: Validate stored receipt schema, exact namespace binding, canonical result digest and input/origin request digest before returning. Reject malformed/corrupt receipts without mutation; do not rebuild them from mutable heads.
